title: Extracting meaningful circuit-based calcium dynamics in astrocytes and neurons from adult mouse brain slices using single-photon GCaMP imaging
protocol: Measure 180 mL of NMDG stock solution and 90 mL of HEPES holding solution.
Mix in 392 mg of N-acetyl-L-cysteine (NAC) to the NMDG solution.
Mix in 196 mg of NAC to the HEPES solution.
Bubble both solutions with a mixture of 95% O₂ and 5% CO₂ for 10 minutes.
Pipette HCl or KOH into the NMDG solution as needed, until pH reaches 7.24.
Pipette HCl or NaOH into the HEPES solution as needed, until pH reaches 7.24.
Adjust osmolarity of both solutions to 300 mOsm using an osmometer.
Reduce osmolarity by adding ddH₂O to the NMDG solution if necessary.
Reduce osmolarity by adding ddH₂O to the HEPES solution if necessary.
Setup dissection tools and vibratome and water bath.
Bring water bath to 35°C.
Assemble large scissors for removing head.
Assemble small scissors for cutting skin and skull.
Assemble blunt forceps.
Assemble spatula.
Assemble single edge razor blade.
Prepare tray and Styrofoam lid for pinning and dissection.
Pack vibratome outer-chamber with ice.
Fill inner-chamber of vibratome with 100 mL of ice-cold NMDG solution.
Bubble inner-chamber with 95% O2 and 5% CO2.
Place remaining 100 mL of ice-cold NMDG in slice-holding chamber.
Keep remaining NMDG on ice.
Bubble slice-holding chamber with 95% O2 and 5% CO2.
Reserve small amount of NMDG for cardiac perfusion.
Anesthetize the research animal according to institutional requirements.
Place inverted 15 mL centrifuge tube containing tissue moistened with isoflurane over animal’s snout.
Pin animal, expose heart, puncture right atrium.
Perfuse ∼10 mL of ice-cold NMDG solution into left ventricle.
Quickly remove head after perfusion.
Open skull and remove brain directly into the ice-cold NMDG.
Let brain sit in NMDG for 1 minute.
Remove brain to a towel and bisect hemispheres.
Block brain for semi-transverse sections with single edge razor blade.
Dab excess liquid from brain on towel.
Glue cut cerebellar side of brain to vibratome plate.
Insert plate into vibratome.
Slice at 280 μm thickness using a speed of ∼ 0.16–0.20 mm/s and an amplitude of 1.6 mm.
Gently collect sections containing hippocampus into a slice holder with ice-cold NMDG using an inverted/cut transfer pipette or gentle paintbrush.
Transfer the NMDG-containing slice holder with sections from the ice to a 35°C water bath.
Continue bubbling in the water bath for 8–10 minutes.
Remove holder from the water bath after ∼ 1.5 hours.
Discard the NMDG solution carefully.
Replace with 20°C–24°C, bubbled HEPES holding solution.
Ensure sections are submerged and loosely separated.
Continue bubbling at 20°C–24°C for 1–1.5 h.
Take care that bubbling is not so vigorous as to cause turbulence/tumbling of the sections.
Continue shielding from light with sheets of aluminum foil.
Reserve glassware, dissection tools, and vibratome for “live tissue only.”
Do not share equipment with lab personnel using fixative or other harsh chemicals.
Thoroughly rinse materials in water and scrub with reserved glassware brush.
Apply 70% ethanol to keep bacteria from growing on tools or slice chambers.
Prepare the 1× ACSF recording solution.
Bubble the ACSF for at least 10 minutes at 20°C–24°C with 95% O₂ and 5% CO₂.
Adjust the pH of ACSF to 7.24.
Adjust osmolarity of ACSF to approximately 305 mOsm.
Begin perfusion of ACSF on the microscope using an IV dripper and flow regulator at a rate of about 1–2 ml/min.
Identify regions to image under the microscope.
Place a single slice in an upright microscope recording chamber.
Secure the slice with a slice anchor.
Locate the dentate gyrus with a 10× air objective.
Switch to a long-working distance water-dipping objective with 40× magnification.
Confirm the presence of mCherry+ virally targeted CCK neurons containing DREADD construct.
Observe green GCaMP expression in neurons or astrocytes.
Note that GCaMP has a low baseline fluorescence, which can be observed as a diffuse green signal.
Observe spread of injected AAV2/5-GCaMP, noting it is not spatially restricted as tightly as AAV2-hM3Dq virus.
Set up an imaging session that acquires data at two different XY stage positions.
Extend the imaging session for several different depths into the slice.
Adjust the number of cycles to last approximately 10 min.
Power the camera and stage.
Start the Micromanager software.
Setup and save a configuration file for interacting with the CCD camera.
Setup and save a configuration file for interacting with the XY stage position.
Setup and save a configuration file for interacting with the Z focus position.
Set camera parameters for 100 ms exposure with no binning.
Open the Multi-Dimensional Acquisition Panel in MicroManager.
Enable “Time Points.”
Set the image count to 210 images, 1 ms interval.
Enable “Z-Stacks (Slices).”
Select “Relative Z” mode.
Enter 0 for “Start Z.”
Enter -60 for “End Z.”
Enter 15 for “Step size.”
Disable “Channels” checkbox.
Enable “Multiple Positions (XY).”
Open the “Stage Position List.”
Start “Live View.”
Turn on the blue LED.
Move the XY Stage to the surface of the slice in a field of view of interest.
Push “Mark” to store it as Position0.
Move the XY Stage to a second, non-overlapping region of the tissue.
Mark it as Position1.
Stop Live View.
Turn off the LED.
Minimize room lights or cover the microscope cage with black cloth.
Allow the slice to equilibrate for 5–10 minutes to reduce mechanical drift.
Recheck positioning to ensure stability of the slice.
Acquire calcium data.
Add baseline drugs, such as 1 μM TTX, for 5–10 minutes.
Turn on the blue LED at the lowest setting that provides reasonable signal.
Push “Acquire!” to start collecting Data_1.
Briefly review the dataset and save it to disk with an appropriate filename.
Add CNO to the ACSF reservoir to begin circuit stimulation of CCK cells.
Wait 10 minutes for drugs to reach the slice and activate DREADD receptors.
Recheck the stage position and focus, readjusting as needed.
Push “Acquire!” to start collecting Data_2.
Save Data_2 with an appropriate filename.
Wash out drugs and change the slice to continue with additional samples.
